title: Mathematics on arXiv — daily notable papers, 2 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; this is an inferred, curated ordering of notable recent papers, not measured popularity. Citation evidence for these very recent papers is limited.

sections.title: A Counterexample to the Alon-Krivelevich Conjecture and a New Lower Bound for Choosability of Bipartite Graphs
sections.abstract: The authors construct bipartite graphs whose list-chromatic number grows faster than any constant multiple of the logarithm of maximum degree, disproving the Alon–Krivelevich conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove an uncolorability criterion for their explicit family and derive choice number at least (1/32-o(1))(ln Δ)^2/(ln ln Δ)^3, hence choice number divided by ln Δ tends to infinity.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite simple bipartite graphs; for integers k≥2 and r²>2(2k−1)ln(2k−1), vertices are copies of the k-subsets of a (2k−1)-set, adjacent when their subsets intersect in at most r elements.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a new preprint's claimed disproof; the construction and proof have not been independently assessed here. Its asymptotic bound is for this construction, not a characterization for all bipartite graphs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The claimed counterexample resolves an explicit longstanding conjecture and gives a quantitative lower bound; the authors combine weighted counting, probability, and a fixed-point argument.

sections.title: Rapid mixing of Potts Glauber dynamics throughout uniqueness
sections.abstract: The authors establish fast-mixing bounds for ferromagnetic Potts sampling across the full high-temperature uniqueness regimes on random regular graphs and lattice cubes or tori, and give a related random-cluster result.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove n polylog(n) mixing with high probability on uniformly random Δ-regular graphs for β<β_u(q,T_Δ), inverse spectral gap n^(1+o(1)) on lattice cubes or tori for β<β_c(q,Z^d), and O(log n) Swendsen–Wang mixing on random regular graphs throughout uniqueness.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Ferromagnetic q-state Potts model, every q; Δ≥3 for random regular graphs and d≥2 for lattice cubes or tori. Temperature is strictly below the stated uniqueness or critical thresholds.
sections.unique_caveat: Results cover the specified random-regular and lattice graph families, not every bounded-degree graph; mixing bounds are asymptotic. The authors disclose assistance from ChatGPT 5.6 and 6.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states threshold-scale results for two graph families and a separate logarithmic-time result for Swendsen–Wang dynamics, and the paper crosses probability, discrete mathematics, and mathematical physics.

sections.title: The Cranston--Li--Su--Wang--Xu (2026) conjecture is true
sections.abstract: The author proves that in every finite graph with all degrees even, the graph of nowhere-zero flows is connected under the conjectured cycle changes, for finite abelian groups of size at least four and for integer flows in the stated range.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves both conjectured connectivity statements for even graphs: all finite abelian groups A with |A|≥4, and integer k-flows for every k≥4; all results are reported formalized in Lean 4 from its standard axioms.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite graphs, loops and parallel edges allowed, in which every vertex has even degree; intermediate flows remain nowhere-zero and moves are cycle changes of the specified nonzero value.
sections.unique_caveat: The Lean artifact supports checking the formalized statements but does not replace scrutiny of whether formal definitions match intended conventions; this recent preprint has not been independently reviewed here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper states a full resolution of a named conjecture and reports a Lean 4 formal proof with public supporting material.

sections.title: Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation
sections.abstract: For rotationally invariant first-passage percolation in dimensions d≥2, the authors prove stretched-exponential concentration of passage time around its time constant, implying a variance upper bound of order n^(1−ε).
sections.claimed_result: The authors bound E[exp(|T_n−μn|/n^(1/2(1−ε)))] by a constant for some ε>0, implying Var(T_n)≤C n^(1−ε); the proof combines scale induction, averaging, and an improved Efron–Stein inequality.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Rotationally invariant first-passage percolation on R^d, d≥2; μ is the time constant and C, ε are model-dependent constants as stated in the paper.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract gives existence, not an explicit value, of the positive exponent ε; conclusions depend on the model's rotational-invariance assumptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result extends a sublinear variance bound described by the authors as previously proved in the planar case to rotationally invariant models in all dimensions d≥2; the listing notes a Lean 4 formalization.

sections.title: The metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4
sections.abstract: The author proves a metric version of multiplicity invariance for complex hypersurface germs under a bi-Lipschitz map, with a tangent-cone singular-locus hypothesis, and obtains embedded bi-Lipschitz invariance in dimensions at most four.
sections.claimed_result: For reduced holomorphic function germs related by a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism of their zero sets, multiplicities agree when every irreducible component of the tangent cone of V(f) has singular locus of dimension at most two; a degree-invariance statement is also proved for certain homogeneous hypersurfaces.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Complex analytic hypersurface germs at the origin; reduced defining functions, a bi-Lipschitz equivalence, and the stated tangent-cone singular-locus bound. The paper says this yields embedded bi-Lipschitz multiplicity invariance for n≤4.
sections.unique_caveat: The dimension-four theorem is conditional on the tangent-cone hypothesis; it does not assert the unrestricted topological Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension four.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives a dimension-four result on an explicit geometric conjecture and links algebraic, complex, and metric geometry.

sections.title: Hedetniemi's conjecture for Shannon OR-capacity: counterexamples and asymptotic separation
sections.abstract: The author constructs graph pairs showing that Shannon OR-capacity of a categorical product can fall below the smaller factor capacity, including examples with an asymptotically large separation.
sections.claimed_result: The author disproves the Shannon OR-capacity analogue of Hedetniemi's conjecture; constructions yield factors of arbitrarily large capacity whose product capacity is subpolynomial in the smaller factor's capacity.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite graphs under categorical product and Shannon OR-capacity; constructions include one complete-graph factor, and one result applies for sufficiently large complete graphs.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract leaves open whether product capacity must still tend to infinity whenever both factor capacities tend to infinity; the construction does not settle that asymptotic question.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives explicit counterexamples to a named capacity identity and an asymptotic separation, with an open endpoint stated in the abstract.

sections.title: An odd version of the Grothendieck--Teichmüller Lie algebra and the odd Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors define an odd graded-Lie-algebra analogue of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra and prove an odd Deligne–Drinfeld statement identifying it with a free graded Lie algebra on one generator of weight three.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the odd Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture: the odd Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra is free graded Lie on one odd generator of weight 3; they consequently compute bottom-degree odd graph cohomology, which is mostly zero.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The odd variant replaces free Lie algebras in even generators with free graded Lie algebras in odd generators; its graph-complex relationship is the odd analogue of the classical one.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated cohomology conclusion concerns the bottom cohomological degree, not a complete computation of odd graph-complex cohomology in every degree.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a conjecture analogue and associated graph-cohomology computation, bridging quantum algebra and algebraic topology.

sections.title: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
sections.abstract: The author constructs spectral majorants and minorants for sets with controlled boundary geometry on compact Riemannian manifolds and applies them to effective equidistribution and conditional motivic Chebotarev–Sato-Tate estimates.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves spectral Beurling–Selberg approximations with controlled coefficients and Hausdorff stability, extends them to certain singular spaces, and derives effective motivic Chebotarev–Sato-Tate estimates under the stated conjectural motivic L-function formalism.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact connected Riemannian manifolds; target sets have boundaries of finite upper Minkowski content. The motivic estimates assume the specified L-function formalism, including the motivic Riemann hypothesis.
sections.unique_caveat: The arithmetic estimates are conditional on conjectural L-function properties; their strength depends on the boundary regularity and uniformity assumptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper cross-lists four mathematical subfields and connects explicit spectral approximation to arithmetic equidistribution, with uniformity under common boundary-content bounds.

sections.title: Baker--Akhiezer sections from Higgs bundles and Landau levels in hyperbolic band theory
sections.abstract: The authors identify lowest-Landau-level states and vortices in a hyperbolic band model with Baker–Akhiezer sections and divisors of rank-two twisted Higgs bundles, explaining the level jump at zero momentum through a limiting process.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify the one-dimensional lowest Landau level at nonzero momentum with Baker–Akhiezer sections and their vortices with divisors; they characterize the two-dimensional zero-momentum level via limiting directions and degeneration to the Hitchin section.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Rank-two O(3)-twisted Higgs bundles on the projective line encoding genus-two hyperbolic crystals, in a uniform magnetic field with two flux quanta.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a first-version, 26-page preprint; the identification is in the stated genus-two model and field setting, not a general classification of hyperbolic band systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper explicitly connects Higgs-bundle algebraic geometry with Landau-level states and hyperbolic band theory and is cross-listed across four areas including math.AG.
